maria: Proposal — add two runtime fields: `min_slo_pct` (percent of requests to keep under SLO) and `quota_floor` (minimum reserved tokens for critical routes). Want feedback before I open an RFC.
pranav: quick q — is `min_slo_pct` per-route or global?
alex: my vote is per-route. Different endpoints have wildly different latency shapes.
maria: per-route. default fallback at service-level if not set. idea is to let routing policy prefer cheaper variants but keep a hard floor of capacity for fast paths.
elise: how does this interact with our existing failover rules? e.g., route_by_cost fallback currently prefers highest-availability model when latency spikes.
maria: good point. plan: routing policy compares predicted p95 vs route.min_slo_pct target; if predicted violation, route is routed to higher tier variants until SLO satisfied (within quota_floor limits).
pranav: sample config snippet?
maria: ```json
{
  "route": "chat.completions",
  "min_slo_pct": 99,
  "quota_floor": 5000,
  "variants": ["gptx-8q","gptx-16"],
  "fallback_policy": "tiered"
}
```
alex: looks fine. But quota_floor units are tokens? requests? needs to be explicit.
maria: tokens. will add `quota_floor_units": "tokens"` to schema.
elise: telemetry concerns — we need a new rollout gauge: % requests meeting route.min_slo_pct, and an alert if route hits quota_floor for N minutes. Otherwise ops won't know we're starving the fast path.
pranav: +1 on the gauge. Also add a dry-run mode for the routing engine so we can preview decisions in the console without actually shifting traffic.
maria: planned. console UX: show a small panel on route detail with "SLO health (live/dry-run)", current quota_floor utilization, and a timeline of fallback activations. Thoughts on layout?
alex: keep it compact. left: gauge + numeric, right: timeline + last-triggered reason. Add a CTA to open an automated rollback if quota_floor has been hit repeatedly.
elise: ops-bot: can you add a check to emit a structured event when fallback engages? we want it in traces, not only logs.
ops-bot: acknowledged. I will emit `routing.fallback.engaged` with fields: route, variant_from, variant_to, reason, timestamp, predicted_p95, actual_p95 (when available). :robot_face:
pranav: compatibility note: we must tolerate older clients that don't include min_slo_pct. Default semantics: treat as 0 (no SLO guarantee). Make sure server-side schema migration is additive only.
maria: yes — server will ignore unknown fields and apply default 0. Will open migration checklist: schema bump, console flag, dry-run on by default for first 48h.
alex: can we add a soft-limit first? i.e., if fallback triggers, don't instantly throttle cheaper variant usage to 0 — gradually shift. avoids big swings.
maria: yep that's the plan: linear ramp over 5 minutes by default, configurable via `ramp_duration_s`.
elise: testing plan: perf team to run a weekend canary with synthetic p95 inflation to validate fallback correctness and dashboard signals. Ops to run a failure-injection drill to ensure rollback CTA works.
maria: I'll coordinate. PR incoming with schema + console mockups. tagging @pranav for API review and @ops-bot for telemetry event shape. :eyes: :shipit:
